tasks.title: Create NEW lazy-derived module harness/symbol_ledger.py (record_symbols + resolve_interfaces)
acceptance_criteria: A brand-new file harness/symbol_ledger.py exists exposing exactly resolve_interfaces(interfaces_spec: str, state_dir: Path) -> str and record_symbols(state_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str].

record_symbols reads state/impl_progress.jsonl at call time, filters rows where phase==accepted and event==auto_commit, opens each referenced committed file, and extracts top-level signatures by reusing harness/ast_enforcer.py (no new parser).
record_symbols returns a fresh dict[str, str] mapping top-level symbol name -> committed signature on every call (lazy, never persisted/cached to disk).
resolve_interfaces returns its interfaces_spec input UNCHANGED on any miss (symbol not derivable, or jsonl missing/empty); it performs NO config-flag gating.
The change lands entirely outside the _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE deny-list, adds no eager record_symbols call to the orchestrator, and modifies no existing class methods.
The oracle from symbol-ledger-oracle passes: python -m pytest tests/harness/test_symbol_ledger.py -q.
tasks.verification_command: python -c "import harness.symbol_ledger as m; assert callable(m.resolve_interfaces) and callable(m.record_symbols)"

spec.objective: Implement the new lazy-derived symbol/interface ledger as a standalone read-only helper module that records the top-level signatures actually committed by accepted tasks and resolves a downstream task's spec.interfaces prose against what upstream siblings really produced.
functional_requirements: Expose record_symbols(state_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str] that opens state_dir/state/impl_progress.jsonl (or the equivalent path layout used by the ledger) and iterates its append-only rows.
Filter to accepted rows only: phase == "accepted" and event == "auto_commit"; ignore all other rows.
For each accepted row, resolve each path in its `files` list relative to state_dir and read the committed file content if it exists.

Extract top-level function signatures by REUSING harness/ast_enforcer.py (_extract_func_name_from_signature, the FunctionDef return-type extraction, and visit_FunctionDef/visit_AsyncFunctionDef) — do not invent a new AST or signature parser.
Return a mapping of top-level symbol name -> its committed signature string, freshly derived on each call (lazy; nothing persisted or cached between calls).

Expose resolve_interfaces(interfaces_spec: str, state_dir: Path) -> str that derives the mapping via record_symbols and rewrites the interfaces_spec prose to the committed signature for any named symbol it can resolve.

resolve_interfaces returns the interfaces_spec input UNCHANGED on any miss: symbol not present in the derived mapping, empty mapping, or missing/empty impl_progress.jsonl; this module performs no flag gating (the staging caller owns that).
Handle malformed/blank jsonl lines, absent files, and an absent ledger file gracefully — never raise; degrade to an empty mapping / unchanged input.
spec.interfaces: exposes `resolve_interfaces(interfaces_spec: str, state_dir: Path) -> str`; exposes `record_symbols(state_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]`
edge_cases: impl_progress.jsonl missing -> record_symbols returns {}; resolve_interfaces returns input unchanged.
No row matches phase==accepted & event==auto_commit -> empty mapping.
A `files` entry points at a path that no longer exists -> skip that file, continue.
A committed file that fails to parse -> skip without raising (extraction yields nothing for it).
interfaces_spec referencing a symbol absent from the mapping -> returned byte-for-byte unchanged.
Duplicate symbol names across accepted rows -> last accepted row wins (deterministic ordering by ledger append order).
non_goals: Do NOT wire resolve_interfaces into the staging/materialization seam (staging_resolve_interfaces owns that).
Do NOT add an eager record_symbols call inside orchestrator._auto_commit_accepted or anywhere in the orchestrator.
Do NOT touch harness/brief_status.py, harness/planner/cli.py, or any _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE deny-list file.
Do NOT add new config flags — the hierarchical_planning.symbol_ledger key already exists and is read by the downstream caller, not here.
Do NOT invent a new AST/signature parser.
spec.implementation_notes: New module = new file (oracle-first): create harness/symbol_ledger.py as a BRAND-NEW FILE; do not edit existing modules and do not modify existing class methods via partial edit. Import and REUSE the extraction primitives in harness/ast_enforcer.py rather than writing a parser. The module is a pure read-derived helper: every call re-reads state/impl_progress.jsonl and the referenced committed files (lazy derivation), persisting nothing. Land entirely OUTSIDE the _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE deny-list (harness/agent_jail.py, harness/dbus_proxy.py, harness/paths.py, harness/git_integration.py, harness/orchestrator.py, harness/interceptors.py, harness/selfheal.py, harness/autowork_daemon.py, services/). Keep verification_command to this child's own oracle (tests/harness/test_symbol_ledger.py) plus hermetic regression files only — never glob tests/planner/, never touch network or pip. [OPERATOR] Create harness/symbol_ledger.py as a single NEW top-level module file (no edits to any existing file; stays OFF the _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE deny-list). Expose exactly resolve_interfaces(interfaces_spec: str, state_dir: Path) -> str and record_symbols(state_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str], lazy-derived from accepted auto_commit rows in state/impl_progress.jsonl, reusing harness/ast_enforcer.py for signature extraction. resolve_interfaces returns its input unchanged on any miss.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Reuse the hermetic fixtures from symbol-ledger-oracle (state/impl_progress.jsonl with accepted auto_commit rows + committed sample .py files under a tmp state_dir), plus malformed-line and missing-file variants. No network/pip; no tests/planner glob.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is a small pure read-derived helper; the bulk of correctness pressure comes from the oracle, so test budget remains weighted above implementation.
